title: Moles and Molarity: Reading Chemistry Recipes
h1: The mole and molarity — Avogadro's number in a bottle
description: One mole is 6.022 × 10²³ particles. Here is how to weigh out a mole, dilute a molar solution, and convert between molarity and mass concentration.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against IUPAC Gold Book and 2019 SI redefinition

hero: The mole is a count. 1 mol = 6.022 × 10²³ particles, whatever those particles are. Everything else in analytical chemistry is downstream of that one number.
body: Chemistry works in moles because reactions happen atom-to-atom, and Avogadro's number is the bridge from countable atoms to weighable grams. Since 2019, the mole is defined by the exact value 6.02214076 × 10²³ — no longer tied to the mass of carbon-12.

> 1 mol = 6.02214076 × 10²³ particles (exact since 2019)
> Molar mass of a compound (g/mol) = sum of atomic masses
> Molarity (M) = mol/L = mmol/mL
> Molality (m) = mol/kg of solvent
> 1 M = 1 mol/L = 1,000 mM = 10⁶ µM

NaCl molar mass = 22.99 + 35.45 = 58.44 g/mol. To make 1 L of 1 M NaCl, dissolve 58.44 g in enough water to reach 1,000 mL total volume. Note: not '1,000 mL of water plus 58.44 g' — the salt displaces some volume.

To dilute a 5 M stock to 250 mL of 0.1 M: V₁ = C₂V₂/C₁ = 0.1 × 250 / 5 = 5 mL of stock diluted to 250 mL. This formula is the workhorse of every analytical protocol. Solvent volume added = 245 mL, but always dilute to the final volume mark, not by adding a fixed volume of solvent.

Molarity depends on volume, which depends on temperature. Molality is per kg of solvent, temperature-independent. Physical chemistry and colligative property calculations use molality. Routine solutions use molarity.

0.9% NaCl (w/v) means 0.9 g NaCl per 100 mL = 9 g/L. Divide by molar mass: 9/58.44 = 0.154 M = 154 mM. This is why '154 mM NaCl' and '0.9% saline' refer to the same solution — they are the same concentration in two units.
1 mol = 6.022 × 10²³. Molar mass in g/mol from the periodic table. Molarity = mol/L. C₁V₁ = C₂V₂ for dilution.

faqs.a: Historical: chosen so 1 mole of C-12 weighs exactly 12 g. Since 2019, the number is fixed by definition and 12 g of C-12 is now measured, not defined.
Analytical concentration ignoring dissociation. For dissolved ionic solids, formality equals the molarity of the formula unit before ionisation.

faqs.q: Is ppm the same as µg/g?
faqs.a: For dilute aqueous solutions where 1 mL ≈ 1 g, 1 ppm ≈ 1 mg/L. For gases, ppm is a mole ratio, not a mass ratio.
